title: Super Micro Raises Q1 Revenue Forecast to $19.5B Beating Estimates by $4B

tickers.name: Super Micro Computer, Inc. Common Stock

summary:
Super Micro Computer shares jumped nearly 13% in after hours trading on Monday after the server manufacturer issued an upbeat preliminary outlook for its opening fiscal quarter. The company now expects first quarter net sales between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion, which exceeds its previous guidance of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion and Wall Street estimates of approximately $15 billion. Adjusted gross margins are also projected to rise to between 12% and 12.5%, compared to a prior forecast of 10.4% to 10.8%.

Management attributed the stronger results to increased demand for AI platforms, GPU clusters, and rack scale systems. These figures are preliminary, and Super Micro is scheduled to release its official final earnings results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 on Nov. 3.

selectedTweets.text:
$SMCI is absolutely EXPLODING in after hours trading, with shares surging nearly 13% after the company delivered a MASSIVE preliminary earnings update.  

The company now expects fiscal Q1 revenue of $18.5 BILLION to $19.5 BILLION, significantly above its previous guidance of $14.5B to $15.5B and Wall Street's expectations of roughly $15B. We're talking about an additional $4 BILLION in expected quarterly revenue at the midpoint, which is absolutely INSANE considering the scale at which Super Micro is already operating.  And what's even more interesting is that gross margins are also expected to improve to 12%-12.5%, compared to the previous outlook of 10.4%-10.8%. This is particularly important because one of the biggest concerns surrounding

$SMCI has been its ability to maintain profitability while aggressively competing for AI server contracts.  Now we're seeing revenue accelerate AND margins improve simultaneously. And I think this is yet another example of just how EXTREME demand for AI infrastructure continues to be. Companies are spending enormous amounts of money deploying AI servers, GPU clusters, and rack scale systems, and Super Micro is directly benefiting from that spending.  Of course, these are preliminary results, and we'll need to see the full financial picture when earnings are officially released on November 3 but for anyone questioning whether the AI infrastructure boom is slowing down, these numbers certainly suggest otherwise.
